expansion:
Uncorrected refractive errors are the correct answer to "most common cause of vision impairment": myopia, hyperopia and astigmatism are extremely common in the general population, and when they are left uncorrected they blur vision without destroying the eye's structure, which is why they outnumber all disease-based causes of visual impairment worldwide combined. This global epidemiological ranking is not stated anywhere in the ophthalmology lecture material searched for this course (not taken from the course material); the lectures on refractive errors define emmetropia and ametropia and describe their optics, but they do not rank refractive error against other causes of vision impairment by prevalence.

Cataract, option A, is a major cause of vision impairment and, in many epidemiological rankings, the leading cause of blindness specifically (as opposed to vision impairment in general, a broader category that also includes milder degrees of visual loss); it is not the single most common cause of vision impairment overall once uncorrected refractive error, which is far more prevalent and generally milder, is counted (not taken from the course material).

Glaucoma, option B, is a major cause of irreversible blindness worldwide because of progressive optic nerve damage, but it is far less prevalent in the general population than uncorrected refractive error and is not ranked as the most common cause of vision impairment overall (not taken from the course material).

Trachoma, option D, is an infectious cause of corneal scarring and blindness that remains endemic in some regions, but it affects a much smaller proportion of the global population than uncorrected refractive error and is not the leading cause of vision impairment worldwide (not taken from the course material).
objective: State that uncorrected refractive error is the most common cause of vision impairment worldwide
